newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Third victim of Melbourne forest fires discovered.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Third victim of Melbourne forest fires discovered.

text.p: Police on Wednesday discovered a third victim of the forest fires which destroyed over 40 homes and ravaged the outer suburbs of Australia's second biggest city, Melbourne.
"A third person has been found deceased," police spokesman Kevin Loomes told Reuters.

He said police located the body in the charred remains of a house in the Dandenong mountain range on Melbourne's eastern fringe, which claimed two victims in their twenties in the early hours of Wednesday morning.
Local media said the three had perished after seeking refuge from the fires in the basement of the home, but police said they were unable to confirm this or details of the latest victim.
Loomes said there were no other reports of missing residents in the scorched area.

The smell of burning timber around Melbourne has begun to dissipate as hundreds of firefighters pull back to let heavy rains mop up the last of the fires, which broke out in heatwave conditions on Melbourne's heavily wooded eastern fringe.
"It's raining, so there's help from heaven. The rain has well and truly doused the situation," Country Fire Authority spokesman Gary McQuade told Reuters.
The fires were among about 10 major, scattered outbreaks in tinder-dry forest this week, forcing the evacuation of at least 800 people from their homes east, west and south of the city.

Firefighters, helped by a cool change in the weather and rain, brought the last of the fires under control in the early hours of Wednesday, as police counted the cost of the state of Victoria's worst outbreak of fire in 14 years.
"It's now the job of mopping up," Loomes said.
"We're quite grateful more lives have not been lost...It certainly is the worst (fire outbreak) since the infamous Ash Wednesday fires," he added.
Seventy-six people died and over 2,400 houses burnt to the ground in the so-called Ash Wednesday forest fires of summer 1983 in Victoria and the neighbouring state of South Australia.

At the height of the Dandenong fires on Tuesday, about 700 firefighters battled six major blazes fuelled by dry northerly winds and forests left parched by several days of temperatures hitting 40 degrees Celsius (104 degrees Fahrenheit).
The cause of the fires was not immediately known. The police arson squad is investigating.
Prime Minister John Howard praised firefighters on Wednesday for risking their own safety to tame the blazes.

"I just want to again thank on behalf of the public those magnificent volunteer and other firefighters who always perform so splendidly and in great danger on an occasion like this," Howard said in a television interview.
